fields.Name: IT165 - Task Graph Security and Saga
fields.Description: Exercises task-graph security envelopes, saga compensation claims, the A2A task store's row boundary, and live dispatcher taint gating with compensation against real MJ: Tasks rows (deterministic, mutating, self-cleaning). TGS1: a submitted graph's parent and every child carry the submitting run's envelope in Task.SecurityEnvelope, and an edit to it on an existing row is refused while an ordinary edit saves. TGS2: of two concurrent compensation rows for one forward step (CompensatesTaskID), exactly one lands. TGS3: the durable A2A store reads a task-graph step's ID as not found and will not write over or cancel it, while an A2A task saves under the 'A2A Task' type and reads back. TGS4: runs a small graph through the real dispatcher on the test DB, asserting that taint from an untrusted action propagates through a Decision step to gate a downstream action, failing the graph and triggering saga compensation of completed compensatable steps. TGS5: a tainted one-step graph whose step is Send Single Message (shipped with Config.disallowWhenTainted) runs through the real dispatcher with MJServer's real TaskGraphActionRunner, which refuses the step with TAINTED_EGRESS_BLOCKED before the action runs. TGS6: a tainted fetch fans out to two Human steps assigned to the submitter; the one the submitter completes through a client CRUD boundary (as the Tasks UI does) records them and its downstream step runs clean, while server code acting as the submitter cannot complete the other, fill in or reassign the person's step, rewrite or rerun the completed fetch, or rewrite the workflow's metadata. TGS7: the same graph with a submitting run, settled through the requests the dispatcher raises: server code cannot create an Approved request for a step or point another answer at one; the submitter's own answer through a client CRUD boundary records them as responder and clears taint, while server code's answer settles its step but records no responder, so its downstream step runs tainted. TGS8: a step force-completed through the debugger while the fetch feeding it is still running leaves the step after it tainted. TGS9: ordinary saves cannot create a workflow, add a step (with or without a StepType) to a real one, retype an ordinary task into one, or add or delete one of its edges; ordinary tasks and their subtasks still save.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Envelopes are on every row and immutable; one compensation per forward step; the A2A store touches only A2A Task rows; live dispatcher gates tainted actions downstream of Decision steps and compensates completed steps; the real action runner refuses a disallowWhenTainted action on a tainted graph; a person's review of a Human step clears taint, and server code completing one, early or not, or answering its request, does not; only the dispatcher raises a workflow step's request.
